newsitem.title: USA: Intel holders ok increase in shares.
newsitem.headline: Intel holders ok increase in shares.

text.p: Intel Corp Wednesday said stockholders approved an increase in total authorized shares to 4.5 billion from the current limit of 1.4 billion shares.
The semiconductor giant also said its three-person executive office has officially shifted titles following the company's annual meeting here.

Under the plan, which was previously announced in January, Craig Barrett, 57, is now president and chief operating officer, moving from executive vice president and chief operating officer. Andrew Grove, 60, is now chairman of the board and chief executive officer, moving from president and chief executive officer. And Gordon Moore, 68, has moved to chairman emeritus from chairman.

Earlier this year, Intel's board of directors declared a two-for-one stock split to be effected as a special stock distribution of one share of common stock for each share of the company's common stock outstanding, subject to approval by the stockholders of the increase in authorized shares.
Stockholders and warrant holders of record on June 10, 1997, will be entitled to one additional share or warrant for each share or warrant held on that date. The payment date will be July 13.

Following the split, each outstanding 1998 step-up warrant will entitle the holder to buy one share of Intel common stock at $20.875, which is one-half of the per-share exercise price previously in effect for the period through March 14, 1998.
